messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing (melting) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clapeyron relation for the ice–water equilibrium (slope ≈ –0.01 °C kPa⁻¹ near 0 °C) gives:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx 0\,^\circ\text{C} + (-0.01\,^\circ\text{C/kPa}) \times 10\,\text{kPa}
= -0.1\,^\circ\text{C}
\]

So the freezing point is roughly **–0.1 °C**.

---

**Why the tool isn’t used**

The provided `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` function only calculates boiling points, not freezing points. Therefore, I performed the calculation manually using the known slope of the ice–water phase boundary.
